report_meta.system: Stripe Global Payments and Revenue and Finance Automation (RFA) System

meta_quotes.quote: Report on Stripe, Inc.’s Description of Its Stripe Global Payments and Revenue and Finance Automation (RFA) System ... Throughout the Period April 1, 2025 to March 31, 2026
SOC 2® - SOC for Service Organizations: Trust Services Criteria – Integrated Type 2 Report Prepared in Accordance with the AICPA SSAE No. 18 and 21 as Amended, and IAASB ISAE 3000 Standards
Non-specified users may not rely on this report and do not acquire any rights against Coalfire Controls, LLC as a result of such access.

3.1.1.quote: Sensitive customer data is encrypted via TLS in transit to ensure data security.
3.1.1.note: Report states TLS but never names a version (no 'TLS 1.2'/'TLS 1.3' anywhere), so no exact dropdown match. Also: 'Traffic between any Stripe device to internal services is encrypted via Transport Layer Security (TLS).' (p. 67)

3.1.2.quote: Amazon Aurora databases ("Aurora DBs") utilize encryption at rest to secure their data using Advanced Encryption Standard (AES)-256.

value: Network segmentation of the cardholder data environment and transaction processing environment (SOC 2 p. 61)
Mandatory multi-factor authentication plus LDAP group membership for production access (p. 60)
Intrusion detection system (IDS) for continuous network monitoring (p. 25)
Weekly external network vulnerability scans plus annual external / semi-annual internal penetration testing (pp. 25, 39)
File integrity monitoring (FIM) and anti-malware on production systems (p. 25)
Daily database backups with real-time replication to a secondary data center (pp. 27, 123)

quotes.quote: the cardholder data environment and transaction processing environment were segmented to prevent unauthorized access to user confidential data
Access to the Stripe production environment requires multi-factor authentication and valid Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP) group membership.
The Company uses an intrusion detection system (IDS) for comprehensive system monitoring.
External network vulnerability scans are performed weekly to identify, quantify, and prioritize vulnerabilities.
the Company performs external penetration testing annually and internal network penetration testing semi-annually
A file integrity monitoring (FIM) tool is utilized to maintain the integrity of the production system.
The Company also implements real-time replication of databases to a secondary data center

absent_notes.3.1.3: Backups are addressed (daily Aurora/RDS backups, p. 123) but the report never states an encryption standard for backups.
absent_notes.3.1.4: No statement on who generates or manages encryption keys; 'key management'/'KMS'/'encryption key' do not appear in the report. Database encryption is partly carved out to AWS/Equinix CSOCs: 'AWS and Equinix should encrypt databases in their control.' (p. 29).
absent_notes.3.1.6: No mention of anonymization anywhere in the report.
absent_notes.3.1.7: No mention of pseudonymization (or tokenization) anywhere in the report.
absent_notes.3.2.1: Report names AWS and Equinix as data-center colocation subservice organizations (p. 17) but never states data-center regions/locations; the Ireland mentions (pp. 14-15) are Stripe legal entities, not hosting locations.
